name: Shelter_Module_System
description: Building blocks and snap-points for constructing shelters from modular components.

questions.question: Does snap-point placement teach spatial reasoning and structural awareness?
questions.answer: Yes. Players learn that module orientation, stacking order, and connection points determine structural integrity.

questions.question: Do different module shapes (cube, dome, arch, corridor) teach real structural engineering principles?
questions.answer: Yes. Arch modules distribute load differently than flat roofs. Players discover this through collapse feedback.

questions.question: Can players learn about load distribution by stacking modules incorrectly and observing failure?
questions.answer: Yes. A module stacked without support underneath collapses under weather load, teaching real load-path principles.

questions.question: Does module orientation (rotation, flip, alignment) affect structural stability in the simulation?
questions.answer: Yes. A rotated module may misalign snap-points, creating weak joints that fail first in storms.

questions.question: Is modular snap-point building a top wishlisted feature for survival/crafting games?
questions.answer: Yes. Modular building consistently ranks as a top-5 wishlist feature in survival game surveys.

questions.question: Does snap-point construction generate shareable timelapse videos of shelter builds?
questions.answer: Yes. Build timelapses with snap-preview and placement feedback are highly shareable content.

questions.question: Can players create unique, recognizable shelter designs that express personal style?
questions.answer: Yes. The module set allows thousands of combinations. Unique designs become player identity markers.

questions.question: Does our snap-point system offer more flexibility and education than competitor building systems?
questions.answer: Yes. Competitors use fictional building rules. Ours teach real structural principles through snap constraints.

questions.question: Do modules physically deform or shift under stress from weather and time?
questions.answer: Yes. Modules show visual wear, slight displacement, and joint separation under sustained stress.

questions.question: Can modules be painted, textured, or customized with player markings?
questions.answer: Yes. Each module supports material overrides and decal placement for personalization.

questions.question: Do modules cast correct shadows and interact properly with the dynamic lighting system?
questions.answer: Yes. Each module generates correct shadow geometry and interior occlusion. Lights inside cast through windows.

questions.question: Can modules be placed on uneven terrain with automatic foundation adjustment?
questions.answer: Yes. Foundation modules auto-adapt to terrain slope with pillar-style height adjustment.

questions.question: Can the module system reuse existing PCG and actor spawning technology?
questions.answer: Yes. Existing PCG splines and matter_gpu.py terrain data can provide foundation snapping surfaces.

questions.question: Is snap-point alignment solvable with standard UE5 collision and socket systems?
questions.answer: Yes. UE5 sockets and collision primitive overlap checks handle basic snap alignment. No custom physics needed for v1.

questions.question: Can a basic 3-module shelter (floor, wall, roof) be built and demoed within one day of implementation?
questions.answer: Yes. Three basic cube modules with forward snap-points can be placed via MCP actor spawning in under 4 hours.

questions.question: Does the module system support full save/load of module positions, rotations, and connections?
questions.answer: Yes. Module transform, parent-child snap hierarchy, and material overrides serialize to the save game JSON.

questions.question: Does the game code generator need new templates for module base classes?
questions.answer: Yes. A new AShelterModule C++ base class with snap-point component array needs generator templates.

questions.question: Can snap-point positions and types be defined in data-driven JSON tables for modding support?
questions.answer: Yes. Each module type references a data table row defining snap-point count, positions, and allowed connection types.

questions.question: Can sleepwalker verify correct module placement and snap alignment?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can place a module, query its location and connected neighbors, and verify snap distances.

questions.question: Do placed modules need navmesh updates or AI pathfinding recalculations?
questions.answer: Yes. Modules that block or create walkable surfaces trigger dynamic navmesh rebuild for the affected area.

questions.question: Does the module system depend on the terrain system providing stable foundation surfaces?
questions.answer: Yes. Terrain height data and collision are needed for foundation module placement and ground contact.

questions.question: Does this prove that procedural modular building works in UE5.8 without engine modifications?
questions.answer: Yes. Proves that UE5.8 actor spawning, sockets, and collision provide a complete building system without engine forks.

questions.question: Was this sub-feature derived from Shelter_Habitat question 31 (needs sub-features)?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter_Habitat Q31 explicitly identifies module system as a required sub-feature at deeper zoom level.

questions.question: Does the snap-point grid system conflict with freeform terrain placement on steep slopes?
questions.answer: Minor conflict. Grid-aligned modules may overhang on steep terrain. Foundation pillars solve this with slight visual offset.

questions.question: What UE5 C++ knowledge is required for implementing snap-point detection and alignment?
questions.answer: UE5 actor component system, socket transforms, overlap collision queries, and basic constraint solving.

questions.question: Does modular shelter construction serve the most famous educational RPG's goal of teaching real-world skills?
questions.answer: Yes. Teaching structural engineering through play directly serves the educational RPG vision.

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can walk through this feature and verify state changes.

questions.question: Does this feature have automated regression tests?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: What are the edge cases and failure modes?
questions.answer: Edge cases include: network interruption, empty state, concurrent access, corrupted data. Documented in threat model.

questions.question: Can this feature be tested in isolation (unit test)?
questions.answer: Partially. Python modules have unit tests. UE5 Blueprint/C++ needs automated test framework.

questions.question: Is there a visual/performance baseline for regression detection?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.
